hints.title: Prefix Sum Aggregation
hints.text: Precalculate prefix sums of both arrays to evaluate arbitrary subarray sums in constant time.

hints.title: Suffix Dynamic Programming
hints.text: Let dp[i] represent the minimum total cost to partition the suffix starting at index i.

hints.title: Transition Formulation
hints.text: For each start index i, iterate through possible end indices j and transition using the prefix sums, index cost weighting, and dp[j + 1].

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def minimumCost(self, nums: list[int], cost: list[int], k: int) -> int:
        n = len(nums)
        prefix_nums = [0] * (n + 1)
        prefix_cost = [0] * (n + 1)

        for i in range(n):
            prefix_nums[i + 1] = prefix_nums[i] + nums[i]
            prefix_cost[i + 1] = prefix_cost[i] + cost[i]

        dp = [float('inf')] * (n + 1)
        dp[n] = 0

        for i in range(n - 1, -1, -1):
            rem_cost = prefix_cost[n] - prefix_cost[i]
            for j in range(i, n):
                cur_nums = prefix_nums[j + 1]
                cur_cost = prefix_cost[j + 1] - prefix_cost[i]
                cand = cur_nums * cur_cost + k * rem_cost + dp[j + 1]
                if cand < dp[i]:
                    dp[i] = cand

        return dp[0]
```

complexity.notes: Dynamic programming evaluates all split points with constant-time range lookups.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Exhaustive recursive partitioning without caching requires exponential time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Prefix sum arrays and DP table use linear memory.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Formulate the suffix DP state and use prefix sums to achieve quadratic time.
